Prevention: Rotate tomato with non- solanaceae crops, e.g. maize.
This disease is seed- borne so plant certified seeds.
Mulch the soil to reduce soil splashing to the fruit.
Water at the base of the plant to keep foliage dry.
Water should be used early in the morning if overhead irrigation is used.
Harvest fruits promptly to avoid over-ripening.
Monitoring: Small, slightly sunken, water-soaked circular spots on fruit that are starting to ripen.
Depressed, enlarged lesions with central darkened portions.
Yellow spots with brown centre on lower leaves which turn yellow and eventually wilt.
Take action when the disease is noted on one plant if wet weather is forecast.
Direct Control: If symptoms are seen early in the season, remove infected plants/ fruits from the field and bury them.
Restrictions: Wear personal protective equipment when spraying pesticides.
Follow instructions on the product label (dosage, PHI, REl, disposal of pesticide waste amongst others).
If using at 250g/L, stock dilute to 10mls per 25
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use), Green band.
Spray with mancozeb-based products if using a 75% concentrate 30-40g per 20
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use), Green band.
If using at 3g/litre concentrate, use 6-14ml/20 litres of water.
If using a product equivalent to 50% metallic copper, use 50-70g/20L water. 10-14 day intervals
